text:
maya: WFH survival story: set up powerline adapters because the office is upstairs and the router is in the basement. had to fish a cable through the attic hatch with fish tape. photo: https://imgur.com/a/powerline-attic (1 pic)
maya: note: avoid catching Christmas lights in the fish tape. not ideal. :grimacing:
josh: legendary. does the powerline throughput hold? curious numbers pls.
maya: ran a quick speedtest after setup:
```
$ speedtest-cli --simple
Ping: 18.2 ms
Download: 52.1 Mbit/s
Upload: 6.8 Mbit/s
```
maya: enough for slack + one webcam. i put the AP on a small shelf in the loft and bridged VLAN to work SSID.
priya: powerline adapters are underrated. also check the circuit: if basement and office are on different breakers, performance tanks.
rory: pro tip: run the adapter on a surge-protected strip that's not paired with a noisy lamp or microwave. interference is real.
maya: good call. moved it off the lamp strip and got more stable pings. also added a short Ethernet patch to the AP and taped it to the rafters. very aesthetic. :sparkles:
josh: poll: what's your weirdest wiring trick? 1) Powerline adapters 2) Fish-taped attic run 3) Ethernet through dryer vent 4) USB-C power extension to router
priya: 2 for me, ran cable through a false ceiling once.
rory: 1 — had a neighbor steal my bandwidth until i locked down the bridge. :laughing:
ops-bot: Reminder: if you modify physical wiring or install in shared spaces, review /office-wfh-guidelines and ensure no building code violations.
maya: filed a quick note with landlord and left the adapters visible. landlord approved. also labeled cables so future me doesn't curse.
josh: must-see photo for the WFH hall of fame, please post the attic-shot.
maya: posting now. if the modem dies, we know where the Christmas lights and i are resting. :evergreen_tree:
